what_its_for: Mechlorethamine is a chemotherapy medicine used to treat a skin condition called mycosis fungoides (a type of skin lymphoma, which is a cancer that affects the skin). It works by killing or slowing the growth of cancer cells in the skin.
how_to_take: This medicine comes as a gel that you apply directly to the affected areas of your skin once a day. Always wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water right after applying it, even if you wore gloves. Apply it to dry skin only — make sure your skin is completely dry before putting it on. Do not get the gel in your eyes, nose, mouth, or private areas. If it accidentally touches these areas, rinse right away with plenty of water for at least 15 minutes. A caregiver applying the gel for you must wear disposable nitrile gloves every single time.
dosing: Apply a thin layer of the gel to all affected skin areas once every day, at the same time each day. Use only the amount your doctor tells you to use. Do not apply more than directed. Your doctor will show you exactly which areas to treat.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember — but only if there are at least 12 hours until your next scheduled dose. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for the one you missed.
storage: Store the gel in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep it in its original tube and keep the cap tightly closed when not in use. Do not freeze. Keep this medicine away from children and pets. Throw away (dispose of) any unused gel properly — ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting the gel on skin that is not being treated. Do not shower, bathe, or swim for at least 4 hours after applying the gel. Avoid letting other people or pets come into contact with treated skin areas. Keep the gel away from your eyes, ears, nose, mouth, and genital area. Avoid using other skin products, lotions, or medicines on treated areas unless your doctor says it is okay. Avoid sun exposure on treated skin — use protective clothing and ask your doctor about sunscreen use.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: severe skin redness, blistering, peeling, or open sores at the application site; signs of a serious skin reaction that spreads beyond the treated area; eye irritation or eye pain if the gel gets in your eyes; signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; fever or signs of infection on the skin. Also call your doctor if skin irritation is very bothersome or does not improve.
when_it_works: It may take several weeks to months before you see improvement in your skin. Everyone responds differently to this medicine. Do not stop using it without talking to your doctor, even if you do not see results right away. Keep all follow-up appointments so your doctor can check how the medicine is working for you.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do not use this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as it can harm an unborn baby or infant. Use effective birth control during treatment. Children: The safety and effectiveness of this medicine in children have not been established. Older adults: Use with caution — older patients may be more sensitive to skin side effects. Always tell your doctor about all other medicines you are taking, including vitamins and supplements.
